resources.summary: Work in small, verifiable steps: change source, compile or reload, reproduce the request, and inspect the result.

resources.title: Understanding Zotonic applications
resources.summary: Know where files belong and how sites and modules fit together.

resources.title: The Zotonic workspace
resources.summary: The checkout is an Erlang umbrella project: one build contains many applications.

resources.summary: These terms describe different parts of the system.

resources.name: developer_naming
resources.title: Application and module names
resources.summary: Use distinct, consistent names so code and assets can be found without ambiguity.

resources.name: developer_source_directories
resources.title: What belongs in src and priv
resources.summary: Use src for compiled Erlang code and priv for application resources.

resources.name: developer_site_configuration
resources.title: Site configuration and enabled modules
resources.summary: A site is identified by its application and priv/zotonic_site configuration. Supported formats include Erlang .config, JSON, and YAML; follow the format already used by the project.

resources.name: developer_module_discovery
resources.title: How Zotonic finds templates, dispatch rules, and assets
resources.summary: Zotonic indexes resources from the site's active modules. A file existing on disk is not enough: its application must be discoverable, and its module must participate in that site.

resources.name: developer_startup_activation
resources.title: Application startup and per-site module activation
resources.summary: OTP application startup concerns the application and its processes. Zotonic module activation concerns the feature within an individual site.

resources.name: developer_runtime_storage
resources.title: Runtime data and uploaded files
resources.summary: Keep runtime data separate from the application's source and static assets.

resources.summary: Run bin/zotonic from the checkout root to see the available commands. Consult this guide's Command-line reference collection for their arguments and effects.

resources.title: Automatic recompilation and file watching
resources.summary: Zotonic's file handler watches source changes when a supported watcher is available. Erlang, templates, dispatch files, and assets have different handlers.

resources.summary: Use bin/zotonic logtail for the configured console log, or select error or crash when those files are available. The command prints the last 500 lines and exits; it does not follow the log continuously.

resources.name: developer_database_shell
resources.title: Test the database connection
resources.summary: Run bin/zotonic connectdb to test a connection using the global Zotonic database configuration. It does not open PostgreSQL’s interactive client and has no site selector in this checkout.

resources.name: developer_collection_templates
resources.title: Templates and page rendering
resources.summary: Build pages from templates, resources, and reusable components.

resources.name: developer_request_path
resources.title: Follow a request to its template
resources.summary: Start with the URL that gives an unexpected result. Check its hostname: Zotonic uses it to select a site before matching the site's dispatch rules.

resources.name: developer_template_selection
resources.title: Find the template used by a page
resources.summary: Enable module#mod_development and open its template tools in the admin. Search for the template name and inspect the selected file and alternatives.

resources.name: developer_template_layout
resources.title: Create a page layout
resources.summary: Use an existing site base template as your starting point. Put shared document structure in the base and page-specific markup in blocks.

resources.name: developer_template_components
resources.title: Reuse markup with includes and categories
resources.summary: Extract repeated markup into a partial and pass its inputs explicitly.

resources.name: developer_template_overrides
resources.title: Override a module template
resources.summary: Find the active template and its path relative to priv/templates. Create the same relative path in your site or another active module with a higher selection priority.

resources.name: developer_resource_links
resources.title: Link to resources and dispatch routes
resources.summary: Use a resource's page URL when linking to content. This lets Zotonic account for its path and language.

resources.name: developer_template_values
resources.title: Display values safely
resources.summary: Resource properties read through m.rsc follow Zotonic's content handling. Query arguments and values returned by custom models do not automatically have the same guarantees.

resources.name: developer_template_media
resources.title: Display images with mediaclasses
resources.summary: Define reusable image sizes in priv/templates/mediaclass.config and use them in image tags. For example, a local mediaclass can constrain an image's width:

resources.name: developer_template_translations
resources.title: Translate interface text
resources.summary: Write the source text in English and mark static interface text for translation.

resources.name: developer_template_cache
resources.title: Cache a template fragment
resources.summary: First measure the work performed by the fragment. Cache a fragment only when you know which inputs and data changes affect its output.

resources.name: developer_asset_build
resources.title: Build and serve frontend assets
resources.summary: Keep source files such as SCSS in priv/lib-src and compiled assets in priv/lib. Use an app-level Makefile that delegates asset work to the source directory's Makefile.

resources.name: developer_collection_content_data
resources.title: Content and data
resources.summary: Read, connect, search, and manage site content from code.

resources.name: developer_site_context
resources.title: Work with a site context
resources.summary: A context carries the site and request-related state used by Zotonic APIs. Pass it through your functions instead of storing one context globally.

resources.name: developer_resource_identifiers
resources.title: Use stable resource names
resources.summary: A resource has a numeric ID within its database. Give application-owned resources a stable name when code needs to find them across installations.

resources.name: developer_resource_properties
resources.title: Read and update resource properties
resources.summary: Use model#rsc for resource access and m_rsc_update for writes. These APIs handle behavior that a direct SQL update would bypass.

resources.name: developer_categories_predicates
resources.title: Model content with categories and predicates
resources.summary: Use a category to describe what a resource is, such as an article or event. Use a predicate to describe a relationship between two resources, such as an author or subject.

resources.name: developer_content_edges
resources.title: Connect resources and preserve order
resources.summary: An edge connects a subject resource to an object resource through a predicate. Use model#edge to inspect and manage these connections.

resources.name: developer_content_search
resources.title: Search for resources
resources.summary: Use model#search and Zotonic's query language for ordinary content searches. Keep the query close to the page's actual task: filter by category, connection, or date, then choose an explicit sort order.

resources.name: developer_media_data
resources.title: Work with uploaded media
resources.summary: A media resource has ordinary content properties and information about its associated file. Use model#media to inspect and manipulate media through Zotonic's normal processing path.

resources.name: developer_datamodel_fixtures
resources.title: Install initial content with a datamodel
resources.summary: Use a datamodel for application-owned categories, predicates, resources, and relationships that must exist when a module is installed.

resources.name: developer_access_control
resources.title: Keep permission checks at the boundary
resources.summary: Use the request context when checking access to data and actions. A hidden button is not an authorization check: callers can invoke a model or endpoint directly.

resources.name: developer_database_queries
resources.title: Add a database query when models are not enough
resources.summary: Prefer Zotonic models for resources and edges. Use z_db for application tables or queries that the model APIs do not cover.

resources.name: developer_import_export
resources.title: Move content between sites
resources.summary: Export structured resource data and record how source resources map to destination resources. Match stable names or URIs deliberately; do not assume that numeric IDs match across sites.

resources.name: developer_collection_reusable_functionality
resources.title: Building reusable functionality
resources.summary: Add modules, models, controllers, and event handlers.

resources.name: developer_create_module
resources.title: Create a reusable module
resources.summary: Create apps_user/zotonic_mod_garden with the following files. This example adds a discoverable module without starting an extra process.

resources.name: developer_extension_points
resources.title: Choose a model, controller, observer, or component
resources.summary: Choose a model, controller, observer, or component.

resources.name: developer_model_api
resources.title: Expose data through a model
resources.summary: Create src/models/m_garden.erl in the Garden module. This complete example exposes a public greeting:

resources.name: developer_controllers
resources.title: Add an HTTP controller
resources.summary: Use controller_template when a dispatch rule only needs to render a template. Write a custom controller when the endpoint needs additional request processing or response behavior.

resources.name: developer_observers
resources.title: Respond to a notification
resources.summary: Find the notification definition and inspect its callers before implementing an observer. The notifier operation determines whether observers collect results, stop at a first result, or fold a value.

resources.name: developer_template_extensions
resources.title: Add a filter or rendering component
resources.summary: Use a filter for a small transformation of an input value. Keep missing and unexpected values predictable, and escape output at the point where it becomes HTML.

resources.name: developer_schema_upgrades
resources.title: Upgrade a module's data schema
resources.summary: Version schema changes through the module's installation and upgrade mechanism. Inspect a module using -mod_schema and manage_schema/2 before adding your own versioned step.

resources.name: developer_background_work
resources.title: Run work outside a request
resources.summary: Use an existing Zotonic task mechanism when it fits the job. Use a supervised worker when the work needs a persistent process with its own lifecycle.

resources.name: developer_collection_browser_apis
resources.title: Browser interaction and APIs
resources.summary: Connect browser actions to server-side behavior.

resources.name: developer_browser_events
resources.title: Handle a browser event with a wire
resources.summary: Use scomp#wire to connect a browser event to an action or a server postback. Give the target element a stable ID within the rendered page.

resources.name: developer_postback_handlers
resources.title: Handle a postback on the server
resources.summary: Set the wire's delegate to the module that handles the event. Implement its exported event/2 callback with a pattern matching the expected event record.

resources.name: developer_forms_validation
resources.title: Validate a form on both sides
resources.summary: Use semantic form controls with labels and meaningful names. Add Zotonic validators for immediate feedback, then validate the submitted values again at the server boundary.

resources.name: developer_browser_messaging
resources.title: Use Cotonic and MQTT for browser messaging
resources.summary: Use the existing Cotonic browser models and Zotonic MQTT bridge when components need to communicate through topics. First identify whether the topic stays inside the browser or crosses to the server.

resources.name: developer_http_api
resources.title: Expose an operation through an API
resources.summary: Start from the site's existing model API or controller patterns. Specify the method, input fields, response shape, and errors before connecting a browser or external client.

resources.name: developer_browser_debugging
resources.title: Diagnose a failed browser interaction
resources.summary: Reproduce one action with the browser console and network panel open. Check for a JavaScript error before the request, a failed request, or a successful response that the page does not apply.

resources.name: developer_collection_development_tools
resources.title: Development tools and debugging
resources.summary: Find the active code, trace a request, and diagnose unexpected behavior.

resources.name: developer_development_tools_overview
resources.title: Choose a development tool
resources.summary: Start with the symptom and use the smallest tool that explains it.

resources.name: developer_enable_development
resources.title: Enable the Development module
resources.summary: Sign in to the local site's admin as an administrator. Open the module management page, find Development (mod_development), and activate it if necessary.

resources.name: developer_live_reload
resources.title: Reload the browser after source changes
resources.summary: Open System → Development and enable live reload. The page also enables separate CSS and JavaScript files when needed.

resources.name: developer_template_trace
resources.title: Trace templates rendered by a request
resources.summary: Open the Development page's Live dependency graph of templates tool. Start a trace for your session, then load the page or path you want to inspect.

resources.name: developer_template_graph
resources.title: Inspect template dependencies
resources.summary: Open Dependency graph of all available templates from the Development page. Use the graph to understand inheritance and include relationships before changing a shared template.

resources.name: developer_template_xref
resources.title: Check template references
resources.summary: Open Cross-reference check of templates in the Development page and run the check. Read each reported reference with the active module set in mind.

resources.name: developer_dispatch_debugging
resources.title: Trace a URL through dispatch
resources.summary: Open the Development page's dispatch tools. Inspect the list of active rules, then trace the path that produces an unexpected result.

resources.name: developer_observer_tools
resources.title: Find registered observers
resources.summary: Open Show an overview of all observers from the Development page. Find the notification and inspect the registered callbacks and their order.

resources.name: developer_database_trace
resources.title: Trace database queries for your session
resources.summary: Enable module#mod_server_storage if the Development page says it is needed for database tracing. On the Development page, enable Trace all database queries for the current session.

resources.name: developer_function_trace
resources.title: Trace a small number of Erlang calls
resources.summary: Open the Development function tracing tool as the admin user. Enter a module, optionally a function, and a small limit on the number of calls.

resources.name: developer_cache_debugging
resources.title: Distinguish stale cache data from stale code
resources.summary: First check which file is selected and whether the changed code compiled. Then repeat the request with the relevant cache disabled or flushed.

resources.name: developer_structured_logging
resources.title: Write logs that explain an operation
resources.summary: Log the operation and its result with structured fields. Include an identifier that helps connect the message to a resource or job, without logging credentials or complete private request data.

resources.name: developer_recompile_rescan
resources.title: Recompile code and refresh discovery
resources.summary: Use compilation for changed Erlang source, loading for changed BEAM files, and an index refresh when new templates or application files are not discovered.

resources.name: developer_development_api
resources.title: Understand the optional development API
resources.summary: The Development page has an option to enable an API for recompiling and rebuilding Zotonic. The model implements actions for recompiling, flushing caches, and refreshing indexes and translations.

resources.name: developer_collection_testing
resources.title: Testing and maintaining applications
resources.summary: Verify behavior and keep changes easy to maintain.

resources.name: developer_testing_strategy
resources.title: Choose checks for a change
resources.summary: Choose checks for a change.

resources.name: developer_testing_erlang
resources.title: Test Erlang behavior with focused examples
resources.summary: Keep domain logic in small functions that accept explicit inputs. Test expected results, boundary values, and meaningful error cases without starting a full site when the function does not need one.

resources.name: developer_testing_templates
resources.title: Check a rendered template
resources.summary: Render the changed page with realistic content. Include missing optional fields, a long title, several list items, and a second language when applicable.

resources.name: developer_testing_permissions
resources.title: Test with different users
resources.summary: Choose roles that exercise the operation's permission boundary: anonymous visitor, limited editor, and administrator. Use separate browser sessions or an explicit test context for each role.

resources.name: developer_testing_upgrades
resources.title: Verify an upgrade before release
resources.summary: Prepare an isolated copy of the previously released application and database. Add representative edited content, then apply the new code and schema changes.

resources.name: developer_maintaining_dependencies
resources.title: Update dependencies deliberately
resources.summary: Change a dependency when you can identify the required fix or feature and the affected callers. Read its version constraints and inspect the resulting lockfile change.

resources.name: developer_collection_configuration_deployment
resources.title: Configuration and deployment
resources.summary: Configure environments, storage, and a repeatable release process.

resources.name: developer_configuration_layers
resources.title: Find the configuration layer to change
resources.summary: Distinguish global Zotonic configuration, Erlang runtime configuration, site configuration files, and module settings stored for a site. Similar setting names can exist at different layers.

resources.name: developer_runtime_config
resources.title: Change a runtime setting deliberately
resources.summary: Use bin/zotonic setconfig only for a global setting that supports a runtime change. The command changes the running configuration and does not save the value in configuration files.

resources.name: developer_environment_settings
resources.title: Keep development and production settings distinct
resources.summary: Keep development and production settings distinct.

resources.name: developer_storage_configuration
resources.title: Configure persistent file storage
resources.summary: Identify where the site's archive files, generated previews, backups, and security files are stored. These have different retention and recovery needs.

resources.name: developer_deployment_workflow
resources.title: Deploy a repeatable release
resources.summary: Record the code revision, build steps, configuration changes, and schema changes for the release. Build and test the same revision in an acceptance environment first.

resources.name: developer_backup_recovery
resources.title: Verify backups by restoring them
resources.summary: Define what must be recovered: database, original media, configuration, and security material. Check which parts the selected backup includes before depending on it.

resources.name: developer_collection_troubleshooting
resources.title: Troubleshooting
resources.summary: Work from a symptom to a focused check and a verified fix.

resources.name: developer_site_not_starting
resources.title: A site does not start
resources.summary: Run bin/zotonic status to distinguish an unavailable node from a stopped or failing site. Inspect the relevant startup log before repeatedly restarting it.

resources.name: developer_module_missing
resources.title: A module is missing from the admin
resources.summary: Check that the module is an Erlang application in a discovered project directory. Confirm the application name, .app.src, main mod_... module, and successful compilation.

resources.name: developer_module_not_active
resources.title: A module is discovered but not active
resources.summary: Open module management for the correct site. Check whether the module is disabled, waiting for a dependency, or failing during startup.

resources.name: developer_changes_not_loaded
resources.title: A saved change does not appear
resources.summary: Check each stage in order: the edited file, build output, loaded application, active module, selected template, and browser response.

resources.name: developer_wrong_route
resources.title: A URL reaches the wrong page
resources.summary: Confirm the hostname, site, and path from the actual request. Use the dispatch trace to see the selected rule and any rewritten path.

resources.name: developer_model_errors
resources.title: A model returns an error or no value
resources.summary: Check the requested path and compare its binary segments with the model callback patterns. Confirm that the callback returns the unused path in the required result structure.

resources.name: developer_missing_media
resources.title: An uploaded image does not display
resources.summary: Check whether the resource has an original file and whether its media information describes that file correctly. Then inspect the preview request in the browser network panel.

resources.name: developer_slow_requests
resources.title: A page is slow
resources.summary: Measure one representative request and identify whether time is spent in the browser, network, or server. Compare an initial request with a repeated request to see the effect of caches.
